troy.lede: Water damage extraction, mold remediation, fire and smoke cleanup, odor elimination, and full post-loss reconstruction for homeowners and businesses across Troy — from Big Beaver Road to the northern subdivisions off Long Lake and South Boulevard.
local: Troy is Oakland County’s largest city by population, and its housing inventory reflects four decades of continuous suburban development. The older ranches and colonials built in the 1960s and 1970s near Big Beaver Road, Maple Road, and the Somerset corridor carry different restoration demands than the larger, more finish-intensive homes built in northern Troy throughout the 1990s and 2000s. Both present real water damage risk — the older stock from aging galvanized supply lines, outdated drain tile, and original plumbing systems; the newer stock from the high density of fully finished basements loaded with hardwood, built-ins, home theaters, and premium mechanicals.

When a finished basement floods in Bayberry Place, Oak River, Northfield Hills, or Crescent Ridge, the damage scope isn’t just structural — it includes contents handling, substrate moisture beneath hardwood and engineered flooring, and cabinet and built-in assessment. We approach every Troy job with that in mind: the scope is written based on what we measure on site, not a standard residential template.

local: Waterford Township spans 36 square miles of Oakland County’s lakes district — a chain of inland lakes including Cass Lake, Elizabeth Lake, Scott Lake, and Maceday Lake define its western half, while its eastern and central areas carry inland subdivisions from the 1960s through 1990s. Properties along the Cass Lake shoreline and Elizabeth Lake corridor sit on year-round saturated soil with elevated water tables — the same lake hydrology challenge that drives West Bloomfield’s restoration profile, just further north. Sump systems on lake-adjacent lots work harder year-round and fail more often because the water table never fully drops.

The township’s significant share of 1960s through 1990s construction means many Waterford homes are in the same aging infrastructure window as Sterling Heights and Southfield — sump pumps, drain tile, and supply lines reaching or past design life.

west-bloomfield.lede: Full-service restoration for West Bloomfield’s lakefront estates, inland subdivisions, and high-value residential properties — water damage, mold remediation, fire and smoke cleanup, odor elimination, and complete post-loss reconstruction.
local: West Bloomfield is Oakland County’s lakes district — Orchard Lake, Pine Lake, Upper Long Lake, Cass Lake, and Walnut Lake are all within or along the township, and the properties along their shorelines sit on year-round saturated soil with elevated water tables that simply don’t exist in inland suburban communities. Lakefront homes on Orchard Lake, Pine Lake, and Upper Long Lake have seawall-adjacent basements and finished walkout lower levels that sit at or near grade with the waterline. When seasonal lake levels rise — particularly during wet springs or following major Metro Detroit storm events — these properties face chronic seepage and hydrostatic intrusion that goes well beyond what a standard sump pump can address.

Inland, the Maple Road and Middlebelt corridor carries 1970s and 1980s subdivision housing, and the Greer Road and Halsted Road area near Marshbank Park contains larger custom builds from the 1990s and 2000s. The entire township sits on glacial soils with high clay content — a drainage condition that slows water movement, extends hydrostatic pressure windows, and contributes to chronic foundation seepage in older basements long after rain events have passed. Restoration in West Bloomfield requires understanding the difference between a lakefront hydrology problem and an inland drainage problem — they look similar on the surface and require different responses.

risk: A finished basement in an inland West Bloomfield subdivision is a standard extraction and drying job when addressed promptly. A finished walkout lower level on an Orchard Lake or Pine Lake property is a different situation entirely. The soil is saturated year-round. The water table is elevated. Ambient moisture from the lake environment keeps the air humidity higher than surrounding areas. Dehumidifiers work harder and run longer. Drying timelines extend past what homeowners — and some contractors — expect.

Hardwood cupping is one of the most common presentations on West Bloomfield lakefront jobs — subfloor saturation from lake-adjacent hydrostatic pressure often causes hardwood to cup before visible water is present on the surface. By the time the floor is noticeably damaged, the subfloor and framing below it have been absorbing moisture for longer than the visible timeline suggests. Consumer dehumidifiers can’t overcome the ambient lake environment. Professional equipment running an extended cycle under daily monitoring is the only approach that actually clears these jobs.
